description:
The plot illustrates the average correct gate rate across embedding layers for four different input types—Character Attention input, Character MLP input, Wiki Attention input, and Wiki MLP input—used in the analysis of embedding quality in Llama intermediate layers. The x-axis represents the embedding layer, ranging from 0 to 30 with labeled ticks at intervals of 5, while the y-axis shows the average correct gate rate, ranging from 0.0 to 1.0 with labeled ticks at intervals of 0.2. The average correct gate rate is defined as the proportion of question embeddings that achieve the maximum inner product with the relevant passage embeddings, computed for each dataset partition consisting of 50 passage samples. The shaded regions around each line represent the standard deviation across 20 dataset partitions, indicating the variability in the measurements.

The blue solid line, corresponding to Character Attention input, starts at approximately 0.2 at layer 0, rises sharply to about 0.8 at layer 5, and then gradually declines to around 0.7 at layer 30. The blue dashed line, representing Character MLP input, begins at about 0.8 at layer 0, peaks slightly above 0.9 at layer 5, and then decreases to approximately 0.85 at layer 30. The red solid line, for Wiki Attention input, starts at 0.2 at layer 0, increases to about 0.8 at layer 5, and then fluctuates between 0.6 and 0.8 until layer 30. The red dashed line, for Wiki MLP input, starts at 0.8 at layer 0, peaks at 0.9 at layer 5, and then decreases to about 0.85 at layer 30. Overall, the MLP input lines (dashed) consistently show higher average correct gate rates compared to the attention input lines (solid), suggesting that embeddings at the input of MLP layers are more effective than those at the input of attention layers. This observation supports the decision to use the last MLP layer input as the embedding in the main experiments of MEGa.
